posture: An empty scan. Nothing published in the 23-24 August window cleared the relevance filter, in NSW or anywhere else. This was a Sunday-into-Monday window, and the NSW channels are all still showing the items the last three digests already captured: SIRA's news channel has not moved past Bulletin Issue 77 of 18 August, the Personal Injury Commission's latest edition remains PIC News No. 101 of 10 August, SafeWork NSW's most recent media release remains the $390,000 Industrial Court penalty of 19 August, and no fresh icare, Industrial Relations Commission, IRO or NSW Treasury release surfaced. Interstate, the only two things in circulation were the Tasmanian scheme review, which this digest logged yesterday and which has consultation running to September, and routine operational notices - WorkCover Queensland's 31 August wage declaration deadline and a WorkSafe ACT health and safety representative event - both of which the jurisdiction weighting rule excludes as routine local news. No verifiable fresh AFR or SMH public headline on Australian workers compensation was found, so no paywalled items are captured. NSW is now in week eight of the reformed regime and the scheme settings recorded across the 28 June - 23 August digests are unchanged: the 1.99% Nominal Insurer target collection rate frozen to 30 June 2028, industry classification rates held for 2026-27, the revised Workers Compensation Guidelines 2026 and the 2026 Market Practice and Premium Guidelines in force, the 25% WPI threshold applying to primary psychological injury claims notified from 1 July 2026, and Megan Main due to take over as SIRA chief executive on 12 October.
summary: Zero items across all eight categories. Publishing empty sections rather than padding the digest with older material: everything that came up in the scan had either already been captured in the 19-23 August digests or failed the relevance and jurisdiction tests. The nearest misses were the Tasmanian scheme review, logged yesterday as inform and still in its terms-of-reference consultation phase, and the Gallagher workforce-trends psychological-claims data point, also logged yesterday - neither has moved. Two methodology notes for the record. First, direct fetching of the regulator sites was unavailable on this run because the sandbox network allowlist does not cover the NSW and interstate government domains, so the scan was conducted through web search across the free source register rather than by RSS-first retrieval; that reduces confidence slightly on very recent items published in the last few hours, and a same-day item posted to a regulator site this morning could plausibly be missed and would then be picked up in tomorrow's run. Second, the manifest continues to carry entries for 19 and 20 August whose digest files are present, but there is no digest for 22 August, which yesterday's run compensated for by widening its window; no gap remains open. Nothing in this window requires a decision from the risk function. The live watch items stay where they were: the 13-week return-to-work rate at a nine-year low, the psychological-claims cost trajectory that the reforms were designed to bend, and the next reform tranche due in October.
